title: The first Decca date and the series of albums
summary: The first album with 'Jump for Joy' and 'Kisses and Jubilation' pleased Milt Gabler and began a series of twenty to thirty albums.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: To sum it up better, that was the begining of a beautiful thing --' recording wise and friendship wise, and a series of albums, running between 20 and 30. We made in the middle twenties, amoung of albums.

We got to the first date at Decca on 57th Street, and did our first album, and they're talking about mutual admiration societies -- ank and Haggard -- Haggard did some arrangements first, I can't remember what was on the first date, but of course that's another research project. We did so many albums. On that first date, there was "Jump for Joy" and "Kisses and Jubilation", and the playbacks were just way beyond what we expected. Of course, Milt Galber was more pleased than he expected, and that was the beginning, as I say, the long series of albums.
